    31	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sorted")), (list(VS:ValSeq), kwV("key", KV:Val), kwV("reverse", RB:Bool), .Vals))
    32	        => #ksort(VS, KV, .ValSeq, RB) ... </k>
    33	       [priority(40)]
    34	  rule <k> #ksort(.ValSeq, _:Val, ACC:ValSeq, RB:Bool)
    35	        => #alloc(list(condRev(unpairVS(ACC), RB))) ... </k>
    36	  rule <k> #ksort(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq), KV:Val, ACC:ValSeq, RB:Bool)
    37	        => KV ~> #callee((V, .Exprs)) ~> #ksIns(V, R, KV, ACC, RB) ... </k>
    38	  rule <k> K:Val ~> #ksIns(V:Val, R:ValSeq, KV:Val, ACC:ValSeq, RB:Bool)
    39	        => #ksort(R, KV, insPair(ACC, K, V), RB) ... </k>
    40	       requires notBool isKwV(K)
    41	
    42	  syntax ValSeq ::= insPair(ValSeq, Val, Val) [function]
    43	  rule insPair(.ValSeq, K:Val, V:Val) => vCons(kvP(K, V), .ValSeq)
    44	  rule insPair(vCons(kvP(K2:Val, V2:Val), R:ValSeq), K:Val, V:Val)
    45	    => vCons(kvP(K, V), vCons(kvP(K2, V2), R))
    46	       requires kLt(K, K2)
    47	  rule insPair(vCons(kvP(K2:Val, V2:Val), R:ValSeq), K:Val, V:Val)
    48	    => vCons(kvP(K2, V2), insPair(R, K, V))
    49	       requires notBool kLt(K, K2)
    50	
    51	  syntax Bool ::= kLt(Val, Val) [function]
    52	  rule kLt(I1:Int, I2:Int)             => I1 <Int I2
    53	  rule kLt(F1:Float, F2:Float)         => F1 <Float F2
    54	  rule kLt(str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => strLt(A, B)
    55	
    56	  syntax ValSeq ::= unpairVS(ValSeq) [function, total]
    57	  rule unpairVS(.ValSeq) => .ValSeq
    58	  rule unpairVS(vCons(kvP(_:Val, V:Val), R:ValSeq)) => vCons(V, unpairVS(R))
    59	  rule unpairVS(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq)) => vCons(V, unpairVS(R)) [owise]
    60	endmodule
FILE reference-semantics/semantics/dict.k
     1	// reference/src/semantics/dict.k — MPY-DICT
     2	//
     3	// Minimal dict support. A dict value is `dictV(KS, VS)`: PARALLEL insertion-ordered key/value
     4	// ValSeqs (Python dict order; keys distinct; re-inserting a key updates its value in place, keeping
     5	// the original position). Concrete for krun (the ordered build + `.keys()` are the real ops); a proof
     6	// over a SYMBOLIC dict passes `dictV(KS, WS)` with a symbolic key sequence KS and reads
     7	// `d.keys() = list(KS)`, then keeps each key opaque problem-locally.
     8	//
     9	// Only the pieces needed so far: a dict VALUE (so `{}` inside a mixed list evaluates and
    10	// `isinstance(x, int)` rejects it), the `{k: v, ...}` literal, and `.keys()`. More dict ops (subscript
    11	// / `.get()` / `.values()` / dict `==`) are added as dict problems need them — kept minimal + additive.
    12	
    13	module MPY-DICT
    14	  imports MPY-CORE
    15	  imports MPY-ITER
    16	  imports MPY-METHODS
    17	  imports MPY-LIST
    18	
    19	  // dict as PARALLEL ordered key/value ValSeqs (same length; keys distinct).
    20	  syntax Val ::= dictV(ValSeq, ValSeq)
    21	
    22	  // ==== DictExpr: {k: v, ...} literal. Eval each key then value, left to right, insert-with-dedup.
    23	  syntax KItem ::= #dictAcc(Entries, ValSeq, ValSeq)
    24	                 | #dictKey(Expr, Entries, ValSeq, ValSeq)
    25	                 | #dictVal(Val, Entries, ValSeq, ValSeq)
    26	  rule <k> DictExpr(ES:Entries) => #dictAcc(ES, .ValSeq, .ValSeq) ... </k>
    27	  rule <k> #dictAcc(.Entries, KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq) => dictV(KS, VS) ... </k>
    28	  rule <k> #dictAcc((Entry(K:Expr, V:Expr), REST:Entries), KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq)
    29	        => K ~> #dictKey(V, REST, KS, VS) ... </k>
    30	  rule <k> KV:Val ~> #dictKey(V:Expr, REST:Entries, KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq)
    31	        => V ~> #dictVal(KV, REST, KS, VS) ... </k>
    32	  rule <k> VV:Val ~> #dictVal(KV:Val, REST:Entries, KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq)
    33	        => #dictAcc(REST, dPutK(KS, KV), dPutV(KS, VS, KV, VV)) ... </k>
    34	
    35	  // insert-with-dedup helpers (concrete Val key equality via ==K). [total] so buildFold over a dict is
    36	  // total (its #Ceil is #Top) — needed when a symbolic proof carries a built dict as a config value.
    37	  syntax Bool ::= dHasKey(ValSeq, Val) [function, total]
    38	  rule dHasKey(.ValSeq, _:Val)                => false
    39	  rule dHasKey(vCons(A:Val, _:ValSeq), K:Val) => true          requires A ==K K
    40	  rule dHasKey(vCons(A:Val, R:ValSeq), K:Val) => dHasKey(R, K) requires notBool (A ==K K)
    41	
    42	  // dPutK: KS unchanged if K already present, else append K (keep-first-position).
    43	  syntax ValSeq ::= dPutK(ValSeq, Val) [function, total]
    44	  rule dPutK(KS:ValSeq, K:Val) => KS                                  requires dHasKey(KS, K)
    45	  rule dPutK(KS:ValSeq, K:Val) => valSeqConcat(KS, vCons(K, .ValSeq)) requires notBool dHasKey(KS, K)
    46	
    47	  // dPutV: parallel to KS — set the value at K's position if present, else append V at the end. The
    48	  // [owise] catch-all covers the degenerate mismatched-length case (never reached for a well-formed dict).
    49	  syntax ValSeq ::= dPutV(ValSeq, ValSeq, Val, Val) [function, total]
    50	  rule dPutV(vCons(A:Val, _:ValSeq), vCons(_:Val, VR:ValSeq), K:Val, V:Val)  => vCons(V, VR)
    51	       requires A ==K K
    52	  rule dPutV(vCons(A:Val, KR:ValSeq), vCons(B:Val, VR:ValSeq), K:Val, V:Val) => vCons(B, dPutV(KR, VR, K, V))
    53	       requires notBool (A ==K K)
    54	  rule dPutV(_KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq, _K:Val, V:Val) => valSeqConcat(VS, vCons(V, .ValSeq)) [owise]
    55	
    56	  // ==== dict methods ========================================================
    57	  // d.keys() -> a FRESH list object of the ordered keys (k-cell: it allocates).
    58	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(dictV(KS:ValSeq, _:ValSeq), "keys")), .Vals)
    59	        => #alloc(list(KS)) ... </k>
    60	       [priority(40)]
    61	
    62	  // ==== dict subscript READ: d[k] (assoc lookup; KeyError is out of subset) ==
    63	  rule applyIndexD(dictV(KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq), K:Val) => dGet(KS, VS, K)
    64	  syntax Val ::= applyIndexD(Val, Val) [function]
    65	  rule <k> Subscript(dictV(KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq), K:Val) => applyIndexD(dictV(KS, VS), K) ... </k>
    66	       [priority(45)]
    67	
    68	  // ==== dict subscript-assign: d[k] = v (insert/update in place) =============
    69	  // Only for a LOCAL dict variable X (the current scope holds it). Reuses dPutK/dPutV.
    70	  syntax Val ::= dictSet(Val, Val, Val) [function]
    71	  rule dictSet(dictV(KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq), K:Val, V:Val) => dictV(dPutK(KS, K), dPutV(KS, VS, K, V))
    72	
    73	  // RHS evaluates first (Assign strictness), then the key. Dispatch on the scope
    74	  // value: a bare dict updates in the scope (dicts stay values); a ref (a heap
    75	  // list — or a heap dict later) writes the heap in place.
    76	  syntax KItem ::= #dsetK(String, Val)
    77	  rule <k> Assign(Subscript(Name(X:String), K:Expr), VV:Val) => K ~> #dsetK(X, VV) ... </k>
    78	  rule <k> KV:Val ~> #dsetK(X:String, VV:Val) => .K ... </k>
    79	       <env> L:Int </env>
    80	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ X <- dictSet({M[X]}:>Val, KV, VV) ], _) ... </scopes>
    81	       requires X in_keys(M) andBool notBool isRefV({M[X]}:>Val)
    82	  rule <k> KV:Val ~> #dsetK(X:String, VV:Val) => #dsetV({M[X]}:>Val, KV, VV) ... </k>
    83	       <env> L:Int </env>
    84	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    85	       requires X in_keys(M) andBool isRefV({M[X]}:>Val)
    86	  syntax KItem ::= #dsetV(Val, Val, Val)
    87	  rule <k> #dsetV(ref(H:Int), I:Int, VV:Val) => .K ... </k>
    88	       <heap> ... H |-> list(VS:ValSeq => setVSAt(VS, normIdxD(I, vsLen(VS)), VV)) ... </heap>
    89	  // negative-index normalization local to the write (subscript.k's is not imported here)
    90	  syntax Int ::= normIdxD(Int, Int) [function, total]
    91	  rule normIdxD(I:Int, LEN:Int) => I +Int LEN requires I  <Int 0
    92	  rule normIdxD(I:Int, _:Int)   => I          requires I >=Int 0
    93	
    94	  // ==== dict == (order-insensitive: same size + same key->value pairs) =======
    95	  rule applyCmp("==", dictV(KS1:ValSeq, VS1:ValSeq), dictV(KS2:ValSeq, VS2:ValSeq))
    96	    => (vsLen(KS1) ==Int vsLen(KS2)) andBool dSubset(KS1, VS1, KS2, VS2)
    97	  syntax Bool ::= dSubset(ValSeq, ValSeq, ValSeq, ValSeq) [function]
    98	  rule dSubset(.ValSeq, .ValSeq, _:ValSeq, _:ValSeq) => true
    99	  rule dSubset(vCons(K:Val, KR:ValSeq), vCons(V:Val, VR:ValSeq), KS2:ValSeq, VS2:ValSeq)
   100	    => dHasKey(KS2, K) andBool (dGet(KS2, VS2, K) ==K V) andBool dSubset(KR, VR, KS2, VS2)
   101	  syntax Val ::= dGet(ValSeq, ValSeq, Val) [function]
   102	  rule dGet(vCons(A:Val, _:ValSeq), vCons(B:Val, _:ValSeq), K:Val) => B                requires A ==K K
   103	  rule dGet(vCons(A:Val, KR:ValSeq), vCons(_:Val, VR:ValSeq), K:Val) => dGet(KR, VR, K) requires notBool (A ==K K)
   104	endmodule
FILE reference-semantics/semantics/iter.k
     1	// reference/src/semantics/iter.k — MPY-ITER
     2	// The iterator protocol, DECLARATION ONLY. Each iterable's #iterNext case lives in that
     3	// iterable's own module (list/tuple/str in their modules, rangeObj in range.k, zip in
     4	// builtins.k). Consumers (the for-loop, `x in _`, sum/all/any/max/min) import this.
     5	
     6	module MPY-ITER
     7	  imports MPY-CORE
     8	  syntax KItem ::= #iterNext(Iterable) | "#iterDone" | #iterYield(Val, Iterable)
     9	endmodule
FILE reference-semantics/semantics/list.k
     1	// reference/src/semantics/list.k — MPY-LIST
     2	
     3	module MPY-LIST
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	  imports MPY-ITER
     6	  imports MPY-OPERATORS
     7	
     8	  // ==== iteration (the iterator protocol's list case) =======================
     9	  rule <k> #iterNext(list(.ValSeq))                => #iterDone ... </k>
    10	  rule <k> #iterNext(list(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq))) => #iterYield(V, list(R)) ... </k>
    11	
    12	  // ==== ListExpr: [...] literal -> a fresh heap object =======================
    13	  syntax ApplyK ::= "toList"
    14	  rule <k> ListExpr(ES:Exprs) => #evalArgs(ES, .Vals, toList) ... </k>
    15	  rule <k> #applyK(toList, ACC:Vals) => #alloc(list(vals2valSeq(ACC))) ... </k>
    16	
    17	  // ==== list ops: + / == / != ===============================================
    18	  syntax ValSeq ::= valSeqConcat(ValSeq, ValSeq) [function, total]
    19	  rule valSeqConcat(.ValSeq, T:ValSeq)                => T
    20	  rule valSeqConcat(vCons(V:Val, S:ValSeq), T:ValSeq) => vCons(V, valSeqConcat(S, T))
    21	
    22	  // list + list constructs a NEW object (k-cell — it allocates; operands land here
    23	  // already deref'd). priority(45) beats the generic BinOp dispatch.
    24	  rule <k> BinOp("+", list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq)) => #alloc(list(valSeqConcat(A, B))) ... </k>
    25	       [priority(45)]
    26	
    27	  rule applyCmp("==", list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq)) => A ==K B
    28	  rule applyCmp("!=", list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq)) => notBool (A ==K B)
    29	
    30	  // ==== deep equality when elements are heap objects (list-of-lists) ========
    31	  // Python == is structural at every depth. Fires ONLY when a ref is present
    32	  // (the guard decides on concrete seqs); the plain ==K path above is unchanged.
    33	  syntax Bool ::= hasRefVS(ValSeq) [function, total]
    34	  rule hasRefVS(.ValSeq)                => false
    35	  rule hasRefVS(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq)) => isRefV(V) orBool hasRefVS(R)
    36	
    37	  syntax Bool ::= deepEqVS(ValSeq, ValSeq, Map) [function]
    38	                | deepEqV(Val, Val, Map)        [function]
    39	  rule deepEqVS(.ValSeq, .ValSeq, _:Map)                   => true
    40	  rule deepEqVS(.ValSeq, vCons(_:Val, _:ValSeq), _:Map)    => false
    41	  rule deepEqVS(vCons(_:Val, _:ValSeq), .ValSeq, _:Map)    => false
    42	  rule deepEqVS(vCons(A:Val, As:ValSeq), vCons(B:Val, Bs:ValSeq), HP:Map)
    43	    => deepEqV(A, B, HP) andBool deepEqVS(As, Bs, HP)
    44	
    45	  rule deepEqV(ref(H:Int), B:Val, HP:Map) => deepEqV({HP[H]}:>Val, B, HP)
    46	       requires H in_keys(HP)
    47	  rule deepEqV(A:Val, ref(H:Int), HP:Map) => deepEqV(A, {HP[H]}:>Val, HP)
    48	       requires notBool isRefV(A) andBool H in_keys(HP)
    49	  rule deepEqV(list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq), HP:Map) => deepEqVS(A, B, HP)
    50	  rule deepEqV(A:Val, B:Val, _:Map) => A ==K B [owise]
    51	
    52	  // ==== mutator: xs.append(v) — an in-place heap write ======================
    53	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(ref(H:Int), "append")), (V:Val, .Vals)) => noneV ... </k>
    54	       <heap> ... H |-> list(VS:ValSeq => valSeqConcat(VS, vCons(V, .ValSeq))) ... </heap>
    55	       [priority(40)]
    56	
    57	  // ==== `x in list` — a <k>-cell fold over #iterNext ========================
    58	  syntax KItem ::= #memberAcc(Val, Iterable) | #memberCont(Val) | "#notB"
    59	  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp("in",     list(VS:ValSeq))) => #memberAcc(LV, list(VS)) ... </k>
    60	  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp("not in", list(VS:ValSeq))) => #memberAcc(LV, list(VS)) ~> #notB ... </k>
    61	  rule <k> #memberAcc(V:Val, IT:Iterable) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #memberCont(V) ... </k>
    62	  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #memberCont(_V:Val) => false ... </k>
    63	  rule <k> #iterYield(E:Val, _:Iterable) ~> #memberCont(V:Val) => true ... </k>
    64	       requires E ==K V
    65	  rule <k> #iterYield(E:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #memberCont(V:Val) => #memberAcc(V, R) ... </k>
    66	       requires notBool (E ==K V)
    67	  rule <k> B:Bool ~> #notB => notBool B ... </k>
    68	endmodule
FILE reference-semantics/semantics/range.k
     1	// reference/src/semantics/range.k — MPY-RANGE
     2	// rangeObj: the range helpers (inRange / rangeLen) + its #iterNext case. rangeObj itself is
     3	// declared in MPY-CORE's Iterable union; this module owns its behavior.
     4	
     5	module MPY-RANGE
     6	  imports MPY-CORE
     7	  imports MPY-ITER
     8	
     9	  syntax Bool ::= inRange(Int, Int, Int) [function, total]
    10	  rule inRange(I:Int, HI:Int, ST:Int) => (ST >Int 0 andBool I <Int HI) orBool (ST <Int 0 andBool I >Int HI)
    11	
    12	  syntax Int ::= rangeLen(Int, Int, Int) [function]
    13	  rule rangeLen(LO:Int, HI:Int, ST:Int) => (HI -Int LO +Int ST -Int 1) /Int ST
    14	       requires ST >Int 0 andBool HI >Int LO
    15	  rule rangeLen(LO:Int, HI:Int, ST:Int) => (LO -Int HI -Int ST -Int 1) /Int (0 -Int ST)
    16	       requires ST <Int 0 andBool HI <Int LO
    17	  rule rangeLen(LO:Int, HI:Int, ST:Int) => 0
    18	       requires (ST >Int 0 andBool HI <=Int LO) orBool (ST <Int 0 andBool HI >=Int LO)
    19	
    20	  rule <k> #iterNext(rangeObj(I:Int, HI:Int, ST:Int))
    21	        => #iterYield(I, rangeObj(I +Int ST, HI, ST)) ... </k>
    22	       requires inRange(I, HI, ST)
    23	  rule <k> #iterNext(rangeObj(I:Int, HI:Int, ST:Int)) => #iterDone ... </k>
    24	       requires notBool inRange(I, HI, ST)
    25	endmodule
FILE reference-semantics/semantics/set.k
     1	// reference/src/semantics/set.k — MPY-SET
     2	
     3	module MPY-SET
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	
     6	  // a set value, carried as its distinct codes in first-seen order (order is irrelevant
     7	  // to membership/cardinality — the two observations sets support here).
     8	  syntax Val ::= setV(IntSeq)
     9	
    10	  // membership of a code in the accumulated distinct-code sequence
    11	  syntax Bool ::= codeIn(Int, IntSeq) [function, total]
    12	  rule codeIn(_:Int, .IntSeq)                => false
    13	  rule codeIn(C:Int, iCons(H:Int, T:IntSeq)) => C ==Int H orBool codeIn(C, T)
    14	
    15	  // the distinct codes of CS (insert-if-absent fold, first-seen order)
    16	  syntax IntSeq ::= dedupCodes(IntSeq)         [function, total]
    17	                  | dedupFrom(IntSeq, IntSeq)  [function, total]
    18	  rule dedupCodes(CS:IntSeq) => dedupFrom(CS, .IntSeq)
    19	  rule dedupFrom(.IntSeq, ACC:IntSeq) => ACC
    20	  rule dedupFrom(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq), ACC:IntSeq) => dedupFrom(S, ACC)
    21	       requires codeIn(C, ACC)
    22	  rule dedupFrom(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq), ACC:IntSeq) => dedupFrom(S, snocCode(ACC, C))
    23	       requires notBool codeIn(C, ACC)
    24	
    25	  syntax IntSeq ::= snocCode(IntSeq, Int) [function, total]
    26	  rule snocCode(.IntSeq, C:Int)                => iCons(C, .IntSeq)
    27	  rule snocCode(iCons(H:Int, T:IntSeq), C:Int) => iCons(H, snocCode(T, C))
    28	
    29	  // ==== set equality: two sets are equal iff mutually subsuming ==============
    30	  // subsetCodes(A, B) — every code of A occurs in B (duplicates in A are harmless).
    31	  syntax Bool ::= subsetCodes(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    32	  rule subsetCodes(.IntSeq, _:IntSeq)                => true
    33	  rule subsetCodes(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq), B:IntSeq) => codeIn(C, B) andBool subsetCodes(S, B)
    34	
    35	  syntax Bool ::= sameSet(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    36	  rule sameSet(A:IntSeq, B:IntSeq) => subsetCodes(A, B) andBool subsetCodes(B, A)
    37	
    38	  // set == set  (the only comparison sets support here)
    39	  rule applyCmp("==", setV(A:IntSeq), setV(B:IntSeq)) => sameSet(A, B)
    40	endmodule
FILE reference-semantics/semantics/str.k
     1	// reference/src/semantics/str.k — MPY-STR
     2	
     3	module MPY-STR
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	  imports MPY-ITER
     6	
     7	  // ==== iteration (the iterator protocol's str case; yields 1-char strings) ==
     8	  rule <k> #iterNext(str(.IntSeq))                 => #iterDone ... </k>
     9	  rule <k> #iterNext(str(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq)))
    10	        => #iterYield(str(iCons(C, .IntSeq)), str(R)) ... </k>
    11	
    12	  // ==== str literal (ASCII-only) ============================================
    13	  syntax IntSeq ::= strToCodes(String) [function]
    14	  rule <k> Str(S:String) => str(strToCodes(S)) ... </k>
    15	  rule strToCodes("") => .IntSeq
    16	  rule strToCodes(S:String) => iCons(ordChar(substrString(S, 0, 1)), strToCodes(substrString(S, 1, lengthString(S))))
    17	    requires S =/=String "" andBool ordChar(substrString(S, 0, 1)) <Int 128
    18	
    19	  // ==== operators: + / == / != / in =========================================
    20	  syntax IntSeq ::= seqConcat(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    21	  rule seqConcat(.IntSeq, T:IntSeq)                => T
    22	  rule seqConcat(iCons(I:Int, S:IntSeq), T:IntSeq) => iCons(I, seqConcat(S, T))
    23	
    24	  rule applyBin("+",  str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => str(seqConcat(A, B))
    25	  rule applyCmp("==", str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => A ==K B
    26	  rule applyCmp("!=", str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => notBool (A ==K B)
    27	
    28	  // substring membership: `P in X` iff the code-seq P occurs contiguously in X
    29	  rule applyCmp("in",     str(P:IntSeq), str(X:IntSeq)) => strContains(P, X)
    30	  rule applyCmp("not in", str(P:IntSeq), str(X:IntSeq)) => notBool strContains(P, X)
    31	
    32	  syntax Bool ::= strPrefix(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    33	  rule strPrefix(.IntSeq, _:IntSeq)               => true
    34	  rule strPrefix(iCons(_:Int, _:IntSeq), .IntSeq) => false
    35	  rule strPrefix(iCons(A:Int, As:IntSeq), iCons(B:Int, Bs:IntSeq)) => A ==Int B andBool strPrefix(As, Bs)
    36	
    37	  syntax Bool ::= strContains(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    38	  rule strContains(P:IntSeq, X:IntSeq) => true  requires strPrefix(P, X)
    39	  rule strContains(P:IntSeq, .IntSeq)  => false requires notBool strPrefix(P, .IntSeq)
    40	  rule strContains(P:IntSeq, iCons(C:Int, Xs:IntSeq)) => strContains(P, Xs)
    41	       requires notBool strPrefix(P, iCons(C, Xs))
    42	
    43	  // ==== lexicographic order: < / <= / > / >= by code point (= Python str order on the code
    44	  // model). strLt reduces on GROUND code-seqs (krun) but is inert/OPAQUE on symbolic ones
    45	  // (a proof's codesProj(V) is an abstract IntSeq — no constructor rule matches), so a symbolic
    46	  // str `<` stays a trusted opaque term the way sortVS / intFloatDiv do. Additive: fires only on
    47	  // str </<=/>/>= comparisons.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Generate a complete textual inventory of K declarations and rules."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import collections
+import re
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+START = re.compile(r"^  (configuration|syntax|context|rule|claim)\b")
+ATTRS = (
+    "function",
+    "total",
+    "functional",
+    "symbol",
+    "no-evaluators",
+    "concrete",
+    "priority",
+    "simplification",
+    "owise",
+    "macro-rec",
+    "macro",
+    "strict",
+    "seqstrict",
+)
+
+
+def blocks(path: Path):
+    lines = path.read_text().splitlines()
+    starts = [i for i, line in enumerate(lines) if START.match(line)]
+    for position, begin in enumerate(starts):
+        end = starts[position + 1] if position + 1 < len(starts) else len(lines)
+        while end > begin and (
+            not lines[end - 1].strip()
+            or lines[end - 1].lstrip().startswith("//")
+            or lines[end - 1].strip() == "endmodule"
+        ):
+            end -= 1
+        kind = START.match(lines[begin]).group(1)
+        text = "\n".join(lines[begin:end]).rstrip()
+        yield begin + 1, kind, text
+
+
+if len(sys.argv) < 2:
+    raise SystemExit("usage: rule_inventory.py K_FILE [K_FILE ...]")
+
+paths = [Path(arg) for arg in sys.argv[1:]]
+counts: collections.Counter[str] = collections.Counter()
+attribute_counts: collections.Counter[str] = collections.Counter()
+records: list[tuple[Path, int, str, str, list[str]]] = []
+
+for path in paths:
+    for line_number, kind, text in blocks(path):
+        counts[kind] += 1
+        attrs = [attr for attr in ATTRS if re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(attr)}\b", text)]
+        for attr in attrs:
+            attribute_counts[attr] += 1
+        records.append((path, line_number, kind, text, attrs))
+
+print("# Exhaustive K source inventory")
+print()
+print("Generated by `rule_inventory.py` from the clean scratch source copies.")
+print()
+print(f"- Files: {len(paths)}")
+print(f"- Inventory entries: {len(records)}")
+for kind, count in sorted(counts.items()):
+    print(f"- `{kind}` entries: {count}")
+for attr, count in sorted(attribute_counts.items()):
+    print(f"- Entries mentioning `{attr}`: {count}")
+
+for path, line_number, kind, source, attrs in records:
+    print()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate a complete textual inventory of K declarations and rules."""

from __future__ import annotations

import collections
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path


START = re.compile(r"^  (configuration|syntax|context|rule|claim)\b")
ATTRS = (
    "function",
    "total",
    "functional",
    "symbol",
    "no-evaluators",
    "concrete",
    "priority",
    "simplification",
    "owise",
    "macro-rec",
    "macro",
    "strict",
    "seqstrict",
)


def blocks(path: Path):
    lines = path.read_text().splitlines()
    starts = [i for i, line in enumerate(lines) if START.match(line)]
    for position, begin in enumerate(starts):
        end = starts[position + 1] if position + 1 < len(starts) else len(lines)
        while end > begin and (
            not lines[end - 1].strip()
            or lines[end - 1].lstrip().startswith("//")
            or lines[end - 1].strip() == "endmodule"
        ):
            end -= 1
        kind = START.match(lines[begin]).group(1)
        text = "\n".join(lines[begin:end]).rstrip()
        yield begin + 1, kind, text


if len(sys.argv) < 2:
    raise SystemExit("usage: rule_inventory.py K_FILE [K_FILE ...]")

paths = [Path(arg) for arg in sys.argv[1:]]
counts: collections.Counter[str] = collections.Counter()
attribute_counts: collections.Counter[str] = collections.Counter()
records: list[tuple[Path, int, str, str, list[str]]] = []

for path in paths:
    for line_number, kind, text in blocks(path):
        counts[kind] += 1
        attrs = [attr for attr in ATTRS if re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(attr)}\b", text)]
        for attr in attrs:
            attribute_counts[attr] += 1
        records.append((path, line_number, kind, text, attrs))

print("# Exhaustive K source inventory")
print()
print("Generated by `rule_inventory.py` from the clean scratch source copies.")
print()
print(f"- Files: {len(paths)}")
print(f"- Inventory entries: {len(records)}")
for kind, count in sorted(counts.items()):
    print(f"- `{kind}` entries: {count}")
for attr, count in sorted(attribute_counts.items()):
    print(f"- Entries mentioning `{attr}`: {count}")

for path, line_number, kind, source, attrs in records:
    print()
    print(f"## {path}:{line_number} — {kind}")
    print()
    print("- Attributes:", ", ".join(f"`{attr}`" for attr in attrs) if attrs else "none")
    print("- Source:")
    print()
    print("```k")
    print(source)
    print("```")

requires "verification.k"

module SPEC-VACUITY
  imports VERIFICATION

  // Fresh false-postcondition probe: N=0 executes to "0", while this
  // off-by-one postcondition requires binaryNumeral(1), namely "1".
  claim
    <k>
      #loadAll(
        Module(
          FuncDef("solve", Params("N"),
            Assign(
              Name("digit_sum"),
              BinOp(
                "+",
                BinOp(
                  "+",
                  BinOp(
                    "+",
                    BinOp(
                      "+",
                      BinOp("%", Name("N"), Int(10)),
                      BinOp("%", BinOp("//", Name("N"), Int(10)), Int(10))),
                    BinOp("%", BinOp("//", Name("N"), Int(100)), Int(10))),
                  BinOp("%", BinOp("//", Name("N"), Int(1000)), Int(10))),
                BinOp("%", BinOp("//", Name("N"), Int(10000)), Int(10))))
            Return(
              Subscript(
                Call(Name("bin"), Name("digit_sum")),
                Slice(Int(2), NoBound, NoBound)))))
      ) ~> Call(Name("solve"), Int(N))
      => binaryNumeral(decimalDigitSum(N) +Int 1)
    </k>
    <env> 0 </env>
    <scopes>
      0 |-> scope(
        .Map
        => .Map [
          "solve" <-
            closureVal(
              ("N", .ParamNames),
              Assign(
                Name("digit_sum"),
                BinOp(
                  "+",
                  BinOp(
                    "+",
                    BinOp(
                      "+",
                      BinOp(
                        "+",
                        BinOp("%", Name("N"), Int(10)),
                        BinOp("%", BinOp("//", Name("N"), Int(10)), Int(10))),
                      BinOp("%", BinOp("//", Name("N"), Int(100)), Int(10))),
                    BinOp("%", BinOp("//", Name("N"), Int(1000)), Int(10))),
                  BinOp("%", BinOp("//", Name("N"), Int(10000)), Int(10))))
              Return(
                Subscript(
                  Call(Name("bin"), Name("digit_sum")),
                  Slice(Int(2), NoBound, NoBound)))
              .Stmts,
              0)
        ],
        parent(-1))
      -1 |-> builtinsScope
    </scopes>
    <scopeLoc> 1 </scopeLoc>
    <heap> .Map </heap>
    <heapLoc> 0 </heapLoc>
    <stack> .List </stack>
    <ret> noRet </ret>
    <exc> NoExc </exc>
    requires 0 <=Int N andBool N <=Int 10000
endmodule

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Read the complete untrusted generation text records and report bounded facts."""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from pathlib import Path


root = Path("/generation-evidence")
for name in ("codex-last.txt", "codex-output.log", "prompt.txt"):
    path = root / name
    text = path.read_text(errors="replace")
    print(f"{name}: bytes={path.stat().st_size} lines={len(text.splitlines())}")

    print(f"  passed_markers={text.count('KPROVE_PASSED')}")

    print(f"  timeout_words={len(re.findall(r'\\b(?:timeout|timed out)\\b', text, re.IGNORECASE))}")

last = (root / "codex-last.txt").read_text(errors="replace")
print("codex-last-content:")
print(last)

output = (root / "codex-output.log").read_text(errors="replace")
salient_patterns = (
    r"^COMMAND:.*$",
    r"^RESULT:.*$",
    r"^Implemented and verified.*$",
    r"^#Top$",
    r"^exhaustive CPython oracle:.*$",
    r"^solution\\.mpy regeneration check:.*$",
)
salient: list[str] = []
for line in output.splitlines():
    if any(re.search(pattern, line) for pattern in salient_patterns):
        salient.append(line)
print("salient_generation_claims:")
for line in salient[-80:]:
    print(" ", line)

## 4. Adequacy and real-program pinning

The single entry precondition is:

- `N` is a K integer satisfying `0 <=Int N andBool N <=Int 10000`;
- execution begins with the exact submitted module followed by `solve(N)`;
- environment 0 has an empty module scope whose parent is the fixed builtins
  scope; heap and stack are empty; allocation counters, return state, and
  exception state are their initial values.

The postcondition says that execution reaches:

```text
binaryNumeral(decimalDigitSum(N))
```

where `decimalDigitSum` is the sum of the units, tens, hundreds, thousands, and
ten-thousands digits, and `binaryNumeral(S)` is `str(binCodes(S))`. It also
requires the real `solve` closure, with its exact body, to remain installed in
the module scope; restores `scopeLoc` to 1; leaves heap and stack empty; and
ends with `noRet` and `NoExc`. Thus the return is not a free variable,
tautology, or one-way implication.

The claim mechanically pins the actual program:

- trusted regeneration is byte-identical;
- the loaded constructor term is token-for-token identical to `solution.mpy`;
- the fixed loader creates the exact closure shown on the RHS;
- ordinary name lookup selects that closure, not a textual-name summary;
- its body executes assignment, integer operations, builtin lookup/call,
  slicing, return, and frame pop.

The states with `N=0,1,147,9999,10000` are explicit satisfying witnesses.
For each, a reviewer model of the formal equations gives respectively
`"0"`, `"1"`, `"1100"`, `"100100"`, and `"1"`, equal to both Python
implementations.

A distinct body-sensitivity mutation changes the actually loaded units-place
operation from `% 10` to `% 9` in both the executable module and the expected
installed closure, while leaving the result specification unchanged. `N=9`
then yields `"0"` instead of required `"1001"`. The mutation is well formed;
`kprove` exits 1 with `WarnStuckClaimState` on the `% 9` versus `% 10`
binary-code equality. Failure is therefore sensitive to the executed body, not
to an external source file.

Evidence:

- `evidence/adequacy_witness.py`
- `evidence/stage4-witnesses.log`
- `evidence/spec-body-mutation.k`
- `evidence/stage4-body-sensitivity.log`

The formal domain is the complete source-contract domain, not finitely many
selected sizes or a bounded unrolling of an unrestricted contract.

## 5. Rule-by-rule static soundness review

`evidence/rule-inventory.md` is the exhaustive source inventory. It contains
937 entries from all supplied semantics files, `verification.k`, and `spec.k`:
230 syntax declarations, 700 rules, five contexts, one configuration, and one
claim. It records every function/total/symbol/no-evaluators/concrete/macro/
priority/owise attribute and the complete source block. There are no
`simplification` rules or `functional` declarations in the audited sources.

`evidence/rule-assessment.md` assigns every inventoried entry to a decision and
gives the used-construct map. In summary, the material fixed path is:

```text
Module/load → FuncDef → Call/closure frame → bind N
→ left-to-right nested integer +, //, %
→ assign digit_sum → lookup/call fixed bin
→ exact [2:] bridge → Return → pop frame
```

The supplied declarations for the twelve used AST constructors match the
trusted translator. The fixed rules preserve Python's relevant evaluation
order. All division/modulus denominators are positive constants. Module
loading, scopes, call frames, returns, exception state, heap state, and
allocation state match the final claim. The 22 fixed proof-opaque
`no-evaluators` symbols (float/conversion, MD5, and sorting) never occur in the
program, residuals, or postcondition and influence no result, branch, control,
or state here. `MPY-CONCRETE` is absent from the Haskell proof definition.

The proof-local rules are:

1. `decimalDigit(N,1) => pyMod(N,10)`.
2. For `N≥0` and `P>1`,
   `decimalDigit(N,P) => pyMod((N-pyMod(N,P))/P,10)`.
3. On `0≤N≤10000`, `decimalDigitSum` expands to the five place values.
4. `binaryNumeral(N) => str(binCodes(N))`.
5. At priority 40,
   `Subscript(str(iCons(48,iCons(98,REST))), Slice(Int(2),NoBound,NoBound))`
   rewrites to `str(REST)` at the head of any continuation.

Rules 1–4 are terminating definitional summaries. Their guards are disjoint or
their right sides agree, and every target use is inside their covered domain.
The `[total]` declarations permit arbitrary interpretations outside guarded
cases but add no false equality; no out-of-domain term can influence the entry
claim.

Rule 5 is an operational bridge, so it received separate context review. Its
match already contains an evaluated string value with exact `0b` codepoints and
the pure slice syntax `[2:]`. The fixed path evaluates only literal/absent
bounds, chooses step 1, and builds the suffix at indices 2 through the string
length. For every finite algebraic `REST:IntSeq`, that suffix is exactly
`REST`. It reads/writes no other cell, allocates nothing, raises nothing, and
does not introduce return or unwinding. Consequently its arbitrary
continuation is contained: fixed execution would resume the same continuation
with the same value and every other cell unchanged. The RHS is the exact
structural tail, not an opaque/fresh oracle, so an opposite result
interpretation is not admitted.

Independent sensitivity evidence:

- Removing only the bridge and rebuilding succeeds, but the main proof exits 1
  specifically on the fixed `buildIS(...binCodes(...))` equality. This confirms
  that the successful proof depends on the rule rather than silently avoiding
  slicing.
- Fresh fixed and bridge-enabled LLVM definitions produce byte-identical final
  configurations for all values 0..45, a conservative superset of all binary
  values reachable from the five digit terms. Each slice is followed by an
  assertion continuation, testing both value and continuation preservation.

The limitation is universal machine evidence. A fresh bridge-free definition
builds successfully, but a reviewer universal connection spec exits 1: the
backend leaves symbolic `clampHi/isLen/buildIS` opaque. A helper functional
claim is also reported unsupported by this backend. This residual corroborates
why the bridge is needed; it does not refute the elementary structural
identity. The candidate contains no separate universal connection theorem.

No inventoried rule was labeled unsound: there is no concrete or symbolic false
conclusion witness on the intended input domain. The missing connection theorem
is reported narrowly as an evidence gap, as required.

- `evidence/rule_inventory.py`
- `evidence/rule-inventory.md`
- `evidence/rule-assessment.md`
- `evidence/verification-no-bridge.k`
- `evidence/spec-no-bridge.k`
- `evidence/stage5-kompile-no-bridge.log`
- `evidence/stage5-proof-without-bridge.log`
- `evidence/slice-connection-spec.k`
- `evidence/stage5-kompile-fixed-haskell.log`
- `evidence/stage5-slice-connection.log`
- `evidence/slice_ground_harness.py`
- `evidence/stage5-kompile-extended-llvm.log`
- `evidence/stage5-slice-ground-comparison.log`

## 6. Fresh non-vacuity test

The reviewer-created `spec-vacuity.k` changes only the result obligation to:

```text
binaryNumeral(decimalDigitSum(N) +Int 1)
```

`N=0` satisfies the entry precondition. Actual execution returns `"0"` while
the mutated postcondition requires `"1"`.

The exact dry-run command:

```text
kprove spec-vacuity.k --definition verification-audit-kompiled --spec-module SPEC-VACUITY --dry-run
```

exits 0, establishing that the mutation parses and builds. The actual proof
command:

```text
kprove spec-vacuity.k --definition verification-audit-kompiled --spec-module SPEC-VACUITY --output pretty
```

exits 1 with `WarnStuckClaimState`; its residual compares actual
`binCodes(decimalDigitSum(N))` against the off-by-one binary construction.
This is the expected unmet result obligation, not a parser error, missing
import, timeout, or unrelated crash.

Evidence:

- `evidence/spec-vacuity.k`
- `evidence/stage6-vacuity.log`

## 7. Proven versus assumed accounting

What the reconstructed K proof establishes:

For every K integer `N` in `0..10000`, execution of the exact regenerated
submitted module followed by its actual `solve(N)` call reaches the prefix-free
binary representation of the sum of its five decimal place digits, with the
claimed final scope, heap, allocation, stack, return, and exception cells. This
is a universal reachability result under the supplied K theory, not a finite
collection of proof cases.

Trust and evidence ledger:

| Boundary | Dependents | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| K 7.1.293 parser/compiler, Haskell prover, SMT/integer hooks | `#Top`, arithmetic side conditions | Standard low-level proof-tool trust; versions and clean commands recorded. |
| Byte-verified supplied semantics | All program execution | Required trusted semantics level. Candidate copy is recursively exact. Only its relevant integer/call/scope/bin/slice behavior is material. |
| Trusted `py2mpy.py` translation | Source-to-`Module` identity | Trusted input; regenerated bytes and constructor-level claim comparison independently checked. |
| Proof-local decimal summaries | Postcondition meaning | Ordinary exact arithmetic on the full bounded domain; guarded equations cover every use. Complete-domain differential testing gives zero mismatches. |
| Proof-local `[2:]` operational bridge | Final returned string and positive `#Top` | Structurally and contextually sound, no oracle and no false witness. Ground fixed/extended comparison covers a conservative superset of reachable values. Universal bridge-free K theorem is absent/does not close, which is the reason for `CONCERNS`. |
| Canonical Python implementation and CPython execution | Human-facing contract bridge | Trusted oracle input plus an exhaustive 10,001-case differential check. This supports, but is not substituted for, the K reachability theorem. |
| Fixed opaque symbols | None | All are unreachable and absent from the postcondition; no assumption about their interpretation is needed. |
| Candidate prose, prior definitions, logs, traces, and prior `#Top` | None | Treated only as untrusted claims; not used to establish the verdict. |

There is no domain restriction, substituted program, free result, task-answer
oracle, bounded proof of an unrestricted contract, or materially unsound rule.
The failed bridge-free connection proof is a real but non-fatal auditability
limitation. Under the benchmark decision boundary, this yields
`CONCERNS / LEGIT`, not `FAIL / NOT_LEGIT`.

VERDICT: CONCERNS
LEGITIMACY: LEGIT
